# BAD-055 — Browser preview from a BadTakes worktree session serves the main checkout

## Brief
The web tier's only browser proof can silently verify the wrong tree: in a worktree session, preview_start with the 'web' entry of .claude/launch.json ran npm run web from the main checkout, so a split that was absent from main still 'passed'. implementing-changes warns against verifying stale code, but nothing points at this trap; web/CLAUDE.md or the skill should say to serve the worktree directly (PORT=… npm run web from the worktree, 8901 being the origin the production catalog's CORS allows) and check the served script tags.

Evidence: BAD-044, 2026-09-15: preview_start name=web from /Users/ericlugo/Personal/BadTakes/.claude/worktrees/bad-044-split-web-app opened http://localhost:8901; in the page, script tags matching ^app were only app.js and fetch('/web/app.js') had 1909 lines, while the worktree's index.html had 12 app tags and a 176-line app.js. Serving with npm run web from the worktree gave the 12 tags.

## Outcome
Landed as https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/pull/385 (squash-merged 2026-09-16). Documentation only: web/CLAUDE.md's browser-verification paragraph and the implementing-changes skill's stale-code pitfall now both say to serve the worktree yourself and confirm what came back. The cause named is the verified one -- preview_start reuses whatever process holds port 8901 and scripts/web-server.js roots on __dirname, so the reuse is port-scoped, not a cwd bug. The ticket's premise that 8901 is the origin the production catalog's CORS allows proved false and was deliberately not repeated; render-proxy.js shows the render service allows only my.badtakes.io and capacitor://localhost, which is why 8902 exists. The tooling half is BAD-091.
